channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Attract 25-30 Million Foreign Tourists Annually
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced that Kyrgyzstan has the potential to host 25 to 30 million foreign tourists annually in the coming years. He also urged judges to make independent decisions, free from fear of national security committee officials. Additionally, plans are underway to relocate the Osh market in Bishkek by March-April 2027, and heating will be supplied to residential buildings starting October 28.

item.title: Resident Accuses Kyrgyz National Security Committee of Seizing 4.5 Million Som
item.description: A resident of Toguz-Toro district has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov, alleging that National Security Committee (GKNb) officials seized 4.5 million som from him without providing a receipt. The man claims the money was taken after he was detained for working with gravel left from a road construction project. He has appealed to the prosecutor's office without resolution.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Law to Reduce Regulatory Burden on Entrepreneurs
item.description: A new law aims to simplify administrative procedures and reduce regulatory burdens for entrepreneurs in Uzbekistan. The changes enhance judicial protection for businesses, streamline account suspension processes, and address excessive administrative procedures that previously caused delays and increased costs.

item.title: Russia may postpone launch of new labor migrant hiring system
item.description: Russia might postpone the launch of its new labor migrant hiring system from January to March 2027, according to sources cited by Kommersant. The system requires foreigners to register with specific employers. Potential delays are attributed to an unfinished bill and lack of a functional digital platform.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Japarov makes historic first official visit to Armenia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov made a historic three-day official visit to Armenia, signing ten agreements and committing to protect Lake Issyk-Kul and Lake Sevan. The visit focused on bilateral cooperation in trade, transit, and friendly relations, aiming to bolster regional stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Abolishes Cinematography Agency, Transfers Functions to Culture Ministry
item.description: Uzbekistan is dissolving the Cinematography Agency and its 19 affiliated organizations, transferring film policy responsibilities to the Ministry of Culture. The agency's ineffectiveness was noted, with performance measured by plan fulfillment rather than film popularity. A new "Uzbekfilm" national film company will be established.

item.title: Uzbekistan Simplifies Customs Procedures to Support Entrepreneurship
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to support entrepreneurship by simplifying customs procedures, according to the State Customs Committee. A presidential decree aims to digitalize the customs system, increase automated clearance, and reduce processing times by half by 2030. Pre-payment based on invoices is now possible for importers.

item.title: Netherlands Plans to Allocate $500 Million for Tropical Forest Conservation
item.description: The Netherlands plans to invest up to $500 million in an international fund for tropical forest conservation over the next decade. The initiative, called the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF), aims for long-term financing for forest-preserving countries. The government is finalizing the mechanism with other nations and the World Bank.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Meets with Emir of Qatar
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, during his working visit. Both leaders noted the strategic partnership between their countries, facilitated by high-level contacts and systematic work. They discussed implementing agreements and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, and social spheres.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Assures Sufficient Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Reserves Until Year-End
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's government has confirmed sufficient reserves of gasoline and diesel fuel to meet domestic demand until the end of the year. Subsidies are being provided to fuel suppliers, with over 11.389 billion soms allocated in the national budget. The cabinet is ensuring uninterrupted supply and addressing logistical issues at the border.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Full Wool Processing Cycle at Tokmok's "Kasiet" Factory
item.description: The "Kasiet" wool processing factory in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, plans to launch a full cycle of domestic wool processing. Deputy Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev visited the facility, which aims to develop a wool cluster. The project includes modern Italian equipment and a three-stage development strategy, focusing on small and medium businesses and primary wool processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan procures only 10% of needed flu vaccines, plans additional purchase
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has purchased only 63,700 doses of flu vaccine, covering about 10% of the over 650,000 citizens at risk. The Ministry of Health plans to acquire an additional 100,000 doses, expected by mid-November, to ensure immunity before the peak season in late November.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tenge: Illusion of Strength Behind Currency Swings
item.description: Experts suggest Kazakhstan's Tenge strength might be an illusion, influenced by state actions, international investors, and global markets, not just oil prices or National Bank decisions. The currency's value depends on dollar supply and demand dynamics, with market participants' timing playing a crucial role.

item.title: Kenyan Parliament Speaker Affirms Adherence to One-China Principle
item.description: Moses Wetangula, Speaker of Kenya's National Assembly, stated in an interview that Kenya upholds the One-China principle. He emphasized that Kenya firmly believes China is a single state and must remain united. Wetangula affirmed his personal commitment, along with the National Assembly and all of Kenya, to this principle.

item.title: New Entry Rules for Uzbekistan Citizens to Egypt Postponed Until March 2027
item.description: The implementation of new entry rules for Uzbek citizens traveling to Egypt has been delayed until March 1, 2027. This decision follows direct negotiations between Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its Cairo embassy with Egyptian authorities. Until the new rules take effect, citizens can travel to Egypt under current regulations.

item.title: Taliban Dismiss Over 200 Prosecutors in Afghanistan Within One Month
item.description: Taliban authorities have dismissed at least 200 prosecutors who served under the previous Afghan government in the past month. Sources indicate that individuals affiliated with the Taliban are being appointed to replace them, with dismissals accelerating following a verbal order from Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Officials to Meet Iran Amid Houthi Attacks
item.description: High-ranking officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are expected to meet in Tehran on October 26 for regional security talks. The meeting aims to reduce tensions and promote dialogue, according to a Saudi official, as part of ongoing efforts within the GCC defense agreement.

item.title: Polio-Free Afghanistan Seeks Continued Support for Global Eradication Efforts
item.description: Polio-Free Afghanistan emphasizes the need for ongoing humanitarian support and cooperation to eradicate polio globally. The organization highlighted the crucial role of donors and partners in strengthening efforts within Afghanistan to vaccinate all remaining unvaccinated children.

item.title: Taliban Allegedly Interfering with Vaccination Efforts in Helmand Province
item.description: World Health Organization and UNICEF officials in Helmand report interference by the Taliban in vaccination programs, causing delays. Sources claim Taliban officials are involved in corruption, influencing recruitment and awareness sessions. Those not affiliated with the Taliban are reportedly barred from participation. Complaints to local authorities have not yet been addressed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reduces Medical Staff Shortage by 20.4% in Five Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has reduced its medical staff shortage by 20.4% over the past five years, with a 28.3% decrease in rural areas. The government has opened 1,003 new medical facilities, including hospitals and clinics, as part of efforts to improve healthcare. The number of doctors benefiting from social support measures has increased significantly, with housing provisions also rising.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Set Cooperation Priorities for 2027-2029
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium aim to enhance cooperation in transport, critical raw materials, agriculture, healthcare, education, and high technologies. Discussions followed the recent visit of the Belgian King and Queen to Kazakhstan, which resulted in a joint statement and numerous agreements. Trade turnover between the two countries has tripled in the last decade.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Republic Day with International Leaders Sending Congratulations
item.description: Kazakhstan observed Republic Day on October 25 with a flag-raising ceremony in Astana. International leaders, including the U.S. Secretary of State, Russian President, and Chinese President, sent congratulatory messages, highlighting strong bilateral relations and cooperation in security and economic spheres.

item.title: Compensation Fully Paid to Victims of 'Dok-1 Maks' and 'Ambronol' Drugs in Uzbekistan
item.description: Compensation has been fully paid by the state to children affected by the drugs 'Dok-1 Maks' and 'Ambronol' between October 20-24, 2026. Parents of affected children confirmed this, and the Prosecutor General's Office confirmed the execution of the court ruling for compensation payments.

item.title: Taliban Finance Ministry Denies Reports of Delayed Salary Payments
item.description: The Taliban Ministry of Finance has refuted claims of delays in salary payments for civilian and military employees, labeling them as rumors. The ministry stated on Monday, October 26, that government employee salaries would be paid on time, despite previous media reports of postponed payments.

item.title: Tajikistan Establishes Minimum Age of 18 for Labor Migrants
item.description: Tajik citizens can now only leave to work abroad starting at age 18. This requirement is enshrined in the new 'Migration' law, which replaces the 1999 law. The age limit also applies to foreign nationals coming to Tajikistan for work. Russia remains the primary destination for Tajik labor migrants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Doubles Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Production Amidst Russian Refinery Issues
item.description: Kyrgyzstan doubled its gasoline and diesel fuel production in January-September compared to the previous year, according to national statistics. This increase comes as Russian refineries face drone attacks, leading to reduced output and import requests. Kyrgyzstan imports over 90% of its petroleum products from Russia.

item.title: Tajikistan Sets 18 as Minimum Age for Labor Migration Under New Law
item.description: A new law in Tajikistan mandates that citizens must be at least 18 years old to engage in labor migration abroad. This age restriction also applies to foreign nationals seeking work in Tajikistan. The law, which replaces one from 1999, aims to protect migrant rights and outlines 14 measures for organizing labor migration to countries other than Russia.

item.title: Ghazni's Bala Hissar Fortress Faces Ruin Amidst Resident Poverty and Repair Ban
item.description: Residents of Ghazni are urging the relocation of families living in the historic Bala Hissar Fortress due to its accelerating decay from neglect, weather, and a ban on repairs. Families cite economic hardship as their reason for staying and claim the Taliban's cultural department prohibits repairs, endangering both residents and the structure. They seek land for relocation or permission to repair their homes.

item.title: Kyzylorda Police Investigate Teenager's Death After Alleged Attack
item.description: The family of a teenager who died from an alleged attack by hooligans in Kyzylorda is demanding a thorough investigation. According to relatives, the boy sustained a fatal wound to the heart. Police have opened two criminal cases, including one for intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm resulting in death and another for failure to fulfill parental duties.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Rises After Five Days of Decline
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased after a five-day period of decline. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 27. The specific rates indicate a rise in the dollar's value.

item.title: US Administration Reportedly Proposes Viktor Orban for UN Secretary-General
item.description: The Trump administration is reportedly considering proposing former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban for the position of UN Secretary-General. The Wall Street Journal cited sources indicating Russia and China might also support this joint candidacy. It remains unclear if Orban has accepted the nomination.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves Quotas for White Sugar Imports for Food Industry
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will introduce quotas for white sugar imports for food industry enterprises, totaling 300,000 tons annually. The quotas are divided among beverage producers (100,000 tons), confectionery manufacturers (100,000 tons), and other food producers (100,000 tons). The government will review quotas every six months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Religious Leader Ismatulla Maksum for Alleged Abuse
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is investigating Ismatulla Maksum, also known as Ismatulla Abdugapar, a Sufi preacher previously convicted of extremism. Reports indicate at least 20 teenagers suffered sexual abuse in a madrassa associated with Maksum. He had previously claimed to be the Mahdi, an Islamic messiah figure.

item.title: Iranians Face Daily Economic Hardship Amidst Sanctions and Inflation
item.description: Many Iranians are struggling with rising living costs, forcing them to re-evaluate expenses and work multiple jobs. Years of international sanctions, persistent inflation, and currency devaluation have severely impacted Iran's economy. This economic pressure, exacerbated by recent conflicts, is a primary driver of public discontent and protests.

item.title: Turkmenistan Questions Relatives of Citizens Suspected of Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: Turkmenistan's security forces are questioning relatives of citizens who migrated to Russia and Ukraine for work. Authorities are investigating whether these individuals are involved in Russia's war in Ukraine. Sources report interrogations are occurring across the country, with officials demanding information and threatening those who do not cooperate.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Discuss Transport Cooperation Prospects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Minister of Transport met with his South Korean counterpart to discuss cooperation in intelligent transport systems, road safety, and railway development. They also focused on enhancing the Middle Corridor's potential and implementing smart traffic solutions like AI-powered traffic management and 'smart' traffic lights.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Citizen Rights and Efficient Problem Resolution
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing the protection of citizens' rights and improving the efficiency of resolving their appeals. Following the principle that government bodies should serve the people, officials conducted outreach in Bukhara, addressing issues related to construction, housing, and utilities, and ensuring accountability for problem-solving.

item.title: Russian Forces Launch Overnight Strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Injuring Four
item.description: Russian forces conducted an overnight air strike on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, injuring at least four people, according to emergency services. Numerous buildings were damaged, including private homes, vehicles, and commercial structures. Fires broke out at impact sites. Reports also indicate Russian strikes in Chernihiv and Khmelnytskyi regions.

item.title: Oman to Lead $500 Million Private Equity Fund for Central Asia and Caucasus
item.description: The Oman Investment Authority will lead a new $500 million private equity fund targeting Central Asia and the Caucasus. The fund, to be managed by an Omani company, will invest in logistics, renewable energy, mining, agriculture, food production, and healthcare. Other partners include China Investment Corporation and Uzbekistan's Fund for Reconstruction and Development.

item.title: Turkmenistan Authorities Remove Satellite Dishes, Seek Starlink Users
item.description: Authorities in Balkanabat, Turkmenistan, have resumed efforts to remove satellite dishes used for internet and television. This is part of a campaign to identify users of the Starlink satellite internet system in a country with poor internet infrastructure. Police are targeting individuals, particularly ethnic Kazakhs, who may have obtained Starlink equipment from neighboring Kazakhstan.
